findings.evidence: Lines 181-185 are followed immediately by `end Polarized` (line 187); the file contains no theorem about uniqueness or spanning — the last declaration is `fromAlternatingCoefficients_isDecomposition` (line 173).
findings.fix: Delete the section, or add the theorem it describes and document the statement, not the proof technique.
findings.issue: Section docstring "## Uniqueness of the decomposition" describes how the existence part of a uniqueness theorem is proved, but no such theorem exists in the file (the PR description's `@[sorryful]` main theorem is not present). It also documents a proof rather than an object.

findings.evidence: roadmap/EpsilonEridaniRoadmaps/SpinStructure/README.md:383-385: "the space of alternating bilinear forms on `V` that are conserved in both slots **and linear in `S`** is exactly two dimensional"; Spin.lean has no `FiniteDimensional`/`finrank` hypothesis anywhere.
findings.fix: Restrict the sentence to alternating forms conserved in both slots *and linear in `S`*, and say plainly that this is not proved here (no dimension hypothesis appears in the file). Line 17 ('span the space of alternating, spin-linear bilinear forms vanishing on `q`') is the same unproved claim.
findings.issue: "Together they span the space of alternating bilinear forms that vanish on `q`. In four dimensions this space is two-dimensional, so `E₁` and `E₂` form a basis" is false as written: alternating forms on a 4-dimensional `V` with ω(q,·)=0 form Λ²((V/⟨q⟩)*), which is 3-dimensional. Two-dimensionality needs the extra restriction to forms linear in `S`. Nothing in the file assumes `dim V = 4` or proves any spanning statement.

findings.evidence: grep for `\.EPS` across `EpsilonEridani/` returns no hit; every use is the bound parameter `(EPS : V [⋀^Fin 4]→ₗ[ℝ] ℝ)` at lines 89, 97, 155, 167.
findings.fix: Either define the structures from `K.EPS` (dropping the parameter), or document the field honestly as currently unconsumed data.
findings.issue: The `SpinKinematics` docstring and the section intro present the `EPS` field as the orientation used by the antisymmetric decomposition, but no declaration in the repository reads `K.EPS`: `structureOne`, `structureTwo`, `IsPolarizedAlternatingDecomposition`, and `fromAlternatingCoefficients` all take an independent `EPS` parameter. The documentation claims a role the field does not have.

findings.evidence: Tensors/Basic.lean:59-67 describes `Hadronic.Witness` as the audit of `IsLorentzCovariant`; Polarized/Kinematics.lean:286 opens it as `Tensors.Hadronic.Witness`.
findings.fix: Replace with the actual reason, already stated accurately in Tensors/Basic.lean:69-75 (an abstract `V` with only a bilinear form has no volume form, so a parity-odd structure needs the four-form as data), and cite that file rather than `Witness`.
findings.issue: "This convention is necessary because `Tensors.Basic.Witness` for the parity-even decomposition has no equivalent in the antisymmetric case without an orientation" misdescribes that section and names it wrongly: the namespace is `Tensors.Hadronic.Witness` (Tensors/Basic.lean:957), and it audits `IsLorentzCovariant` on explicit witness kinematics — it is not an orientation-fixing device for the parity-even decomposition.

findings.evidence: Definitions at lines 89 and 97 both contract the same `EPS`; roadmap README.md:142-143 speaks of "the relative sign of the `g₁` and `g₂` structures and the overall sign of the asymmetries".
findings.fix: State that the overall sign of both coefficients (and of the asymmetries built from them) depends on the chosen orientation.
findings.issue: "Fixing it once fixes the sign of `g₂` and the overall sign of the asymmetries" (repeated in the field docstring, line 77) is wrong: both `E₁` and `E₂` are linear in `EPS`, so `EPS ↦ -EPS` flips `g₁` and `g₂` alike; the orientation cannot fix `g₂`'s sign alone. It is an unadapted paraphrase of the roadmap sentence about the relative sign of the two structures.

findings.evidence: Lines 16, 42, 63-64, 70 of the file; the numbering tracks roadmap/EpsilonEridaniRoadmaps/SpinStructure/README.md section 0.2 and Convention 4, which renumber when the roadmap is reorganised.

findings.issue: Roadmap layer numbering and convention numbering appear in docstrings: line 16 ("Layer 0.2 of the SpinStructure roadmap" + URL), line 42 ("Convention 4 (orientation)"), line 63 ("Layer 0 needs both ... (Convention 4)"), line 70 ("the kinematic record ... of Layer 0.2").

summary: The module docstring states a spanning/basis result the file neither states nor can state (and drops the S-linearity qualifier that makes it true), a trailing section docstring describes the proof of a uniqueness theorem that is absent from the file, and several docstrings carry roadmap layer/convention numbering, a wrong cross-reference, and a garbled orientation-sign claim.
